title: Planaria adapt to barium by changing expression of only a handful of genes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planaria adapt to barium by changing expression of only a handful of genes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Planaria exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker that is evolutionarily novel to them, first lose their heads but then regrow barium-insensitive heads, with only a handful of genes up- or down-regulated, showing that cells can navigate transcriptional space to solve a problem for which there was no selection.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Multiple modalities for computation and control across scales

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Transcriptional analysis reveals that these tissues up- and down-regulate just a handful of genes to get back to physiological and anatomical setpoints despite the inability to regulate potassium.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Multiple modalities for computation and control across scales”. Scope: Planarians cultured in barium chloride

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The anatomical trajectory and expression count are standard measurable outcomes, and public expression archives are plausible direct resources. They test the narrow experimental result well but not the stronger claim of purposive navigation or absence of relevant prior selection.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Analyze survival, head loss and regrowth under barium together with differential expression before and after adaptation, using preregistered thresholds for the number and magnitude of changed genes. Compare with untreated and acute-stress controls to identify changes associated specifically with restored morphology.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No prior selection for barium is a historical inference.

Expression changes may miss protein and physiological regulation.

'Handful' depends on statistical thresholds and sampling time.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The expression half is directly in a public series and can be recounted with ordinary differential-expression methods. That recount can support or refute a small gene list, which is only part of the statement. Head loss and barium-insensitive regrowth, and the reading that cells thereby solved an unselected problem, are not variables in the count matrix and are not discriminated from a generic stress transcriptome.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reanalyze the Dugesia japonica barium RNA-seq with a pre-specified handful rule, for example fewer than 20 genes at FDR under 0.05 and a stated fold change, in heads that regenerated in BaCl2 versus controls. A count under that cutoff would support the transcriptional clause; a count of dozens or hundreds would refute a handful.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A handful is undefined until a threshold is fixed, and the original paper used a stringent fold-change cutoff.

Pooled or few samples limit the stability of the gene list, and the anatomical time course is not in the expression matrix.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.85
discriminating power: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.72
